Which he was. I do not concede the argument.|Motti, unrepentant after being force choked by Darth Vader|{{StoryCite|story=An Incident Report|book=From a Certain Point of View}}}} '''Conan Antonio Motti''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[bureaucrat]] and military [[officer]] who served as an [[admiral]] and [[naval chief]] for the [[Galactic Empire]], the [[Fascism|fascistic]] [[Proclamation of the New Order|successor]] state of the [[Galactic Republic]]. Born into an influential and wealthy family on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] of [[Seswenna]], Motti became a highly decorated [[starship]] captain. By [[14 BBY]], he had swiftly risen through the ranks of [[flag officer]]s and was acting as a naval chief, representing the [[Imperial Navy]] on the [[Joint Chiefs of the Imperial Military]]. [[Commander]] of the [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Steel Talon]]'', Motti became an ally of [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], one of the Empire's most powerful leaders. By the [[time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War]], Motti had elevated to the position of [[Vice Admiral]], [[Chief of the Imperial Navy]], [[Admiral of the Fleet|Admiral of the Navy]], leader of [[Navy|naval]] operations for the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]], and commander of the [[Death Star's Imperial Navy garrison]] and [[Death Star's fleet|fleet]]. A staunch believer in the capabilities of the [[Death Star]], Motti viewed the [[battle station]] as invulnerable and was dismissive of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]'s purported threat to the station. His confidence led to confrontations with several colleagues, such as [[General]] [[Cassio Tagge]] and [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]; during one meeting of the Joint Chiefs, Motti's outbursts in chastising the [[Sith Lord]]'s failures led to him being [[force choke]]d. Motti bristled at the episode and formally protested Vader's actions. Motti's ambitions, which grew in the wake of the battle station's completion, were short-lived, however. The Rebel Alliance, who had obtained a copy of the [[Death Star plans]] during the [[Battle of Scarif]], discovered a weak spot in the station's [[thermal exhaust port]] and successfully [[Battle of Yavin|exploited]] it, leading to the destruction of the battle station along with the deaths of everyone onboard, Motti included. ==Biography== ===Early life and career=== {{Quote|Any attack made by the rebels against this station would be a useless gesture, no matter what technical data they've obtained. This station is now the ultimate power in the universe! I suggest we use it."
"Don't be too proud of this technological terror you've constructed. The ability to destroy a planet is insignificant next to the power of the Force.|Motti and Darth Vader|}} [[File:Motti2.png|thumb|left|300px|Conan Antonio Motti rose through the ranks of the Imperial Navy.]] Conan Antonio Motti was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who hailed from a wealthy and powerful family in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. A [[Homeworld|native]] of the [[planet]] [[Seswenna]], Motti was a [[Imperial officer|naval officer]] in the [[Galactic Empire]], the [[Fascism|fascistic]] [[Proclamation of the New Order|successor]] state of the [[Galactic Republic]] that was governed by [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] on its [[capital]] planet of [[Coruscant]]. He became one of the [[Imperial Navy]]'s most highly decorated [[starship]] [[captain]]s and veteran naval [[commander]]s,''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'' eventually rising to the [[Military rank|rank]] of [[Rear Admiral|rear admiral]] with his flag on the [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Steel Talon]]''.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' By [[14 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] to [[14 BBY]]. Motti was a prominent member of the [[Joint Chiefs of the Imperial Military]]—a collection of [[general]]s, [[admiral]]s, and other [[Senior officer|senior military officers]] that advised the [[Emperor]] on all martial-related matters—and was considered by the Emperor to be a potential candidate for the newly-created position of [[Grand Moff]], a position which would eventually go to [[Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]]. Along with the rest of the Joint Chiefs on Coruscant, Motti helped coordinate the Imperial response to the [[Berch Teller campaign|rebel campaign]] of [[Berch Teller]], a disaffected intelligence analyst whose [[Berch Teller's rebel cell|cell]] threatened various Imperial outposts across the Outer Rim. Due to his involvement, as well as the discrediting of the head of the [[Naval Intelligence Agency]], [[Vice Admiral]] [[Dodd Rancit]], Motti received a promotion from the Emperor[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] to [[Vice Admiral]].[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]] identifies the [[Rank insignia plaque]] that Motti wears in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope]] as the Rank insignia plaque of a [[Vice Admiral]]. Therefore, Motti must be a Vice Admiral ===Death Star command=== ====Testing the superweapon==== {{Quote|Abort."
"I-I'm sorry, sir…"
"Terminate the simulation.|Grand Moff Tarkin and Admiral Motti following the Death Star's failed simulation|[[Age of Rebellion - Grand Moff Tarkin 1|''Age of Rebellion - Grand Moff Tarkin'' 1]]}} [[File:RangoTan-AORTarkin1.jpg|thumb|right|275px|Admiral Motti reporting on Rango Tan.]] By [[1 BBY]],{{FilmDate|IV|1}} Motti held the title of [[Admiral of the Fleet|Admiral of the Navy]]{{EncyclopediaCite|Imperial Officers and Agents}} and was also [[Chief of the Imperial Navy]].''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' Stationed on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]], the Empire's planet-destroying [[battle station]], Motti served as head of naval operations{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Admiral Motti - Imperial Officer}} and assisted Grand Moff Tarkin in testing the [[superweapon]] on the planet [[Rango Tan]], home to an indigenous pre-[[hyperdrive]] species known as [[Rangan]]. After Motti informed the crew of the planet's inhabitants and its lack of involvement in recent conflicts, Tarkin ordered the planet to be destroyed. Before the firing sequence could be completed, however, the simulation failed, and Tarkin demanded it be aborted. When Motti asked what happened, a crew member explained that each [[gunner]] needed to execute his protocol at the right time if the simulation was to be successful. Motti proposed to immediately investigate and detect who had failed to complete the protocol, but Tarkin demanded to see the gunners himself. ====Conference with Darth Vader==== {{Quote|Don't try to frighten us with your sorcerer's ways, Lord Vader! Your sad devotion to that ancient religion has not helped you conjure up the stolen data tapes, or given you clairvoyance enough to find the rebels' hidden fort—"
"I find your lack of faith disturbing.|Darth Vader force chokes Conan Antonio Motti|}} [[File:I_find_your_lack_of_faith_disturbing.png|thumb|300px|Vader Force chokes Motti for his lack of faith.|left]] Having escalated their operations to [[Galactic Civil War|open warfare]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] managed to steal the [[Death Star plans|technical readouts]] of the Death Star during the [[Battle of Scarif]]. [[Darth]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Vader]], a [[Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Secret mission to Tatooine|captured]] the rebel flagship that carried the plans, the ''[[Tantive IV]]'', but was unable to recover the plans themselves. Shortly thereafter, Motti met with [[General]] [[Cassio Tagge]] of the [[Imperial Army]] in his private office onboard the battle station, where the latter was reviewing data from the attack on [[Scarif]]. The two then headed to the [[Death Star conference room|Joint Chiefs' conference room]]. After a senior adviser asked if something was wrong, Motti declared that the theft of the station's plans had made Tagge paranoid.{{StoryCite|story=Fully Operational (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}} In return, Tagge asserted that, until the Death Star was fully operational, the Empire was vulnerable to the Alliance's attacks. Motti, however, retorted that, while the Alliance posed a threat to Tagge's forces, there was no such threat to the battle station. Tagge further argued the Alliance would continue to gain support in the [[Imperial Senate]], but was interrupted by Tarkin, who arrived with [[Lord]] Vader and informed the [[Imperial officer|officers]] present that the Emperor had just dissolved the Senate. He continued to say that fear, in particular fear of the Death Star, would keep [[star system]]s in line, prompting Motti to smile. Tagge brought up the threat of the Alliance, who, due to their possession of the Death Star plans, could discover and exploit a weakness in the battle station, but Vader—who had arrived to interrogate [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan]]—proclaimed that the Empire would soon have the plans once again. Motti stated that, regardless of whatever technical data the Alliance had, any attack on the Death Star would be futile, gloating that the station was the ultimate power in [[Universe|the universe]] and adding that the Empire ought to use it. Vader, however, rebutted this claim, warning Motti not to underestimate the power of [[the Force]]. Arrogance clouding his judgment, Motti mocked Vader, insulting his devotion to the Force, alleging that it had not helped him recover the stolen Death Star plans or locate the Rebels' [[Massassi Site|hidden base]]. In response, Vader began to [[force choke]] the admiral while rebuking him for his "lack of faith," relenting only at Tarkin's insistence. Motti slumped across the conference table, gasping for breath and considerably unnerved, exchanging eye contact with Tagge. Nevertheless, he later submitted a sharply worded incident report criticizing what he characterized as Vader's attempt at religious proselytization, further stressing his confidence and his pride in the battle station. ====Destruction of Alderaan==== {{Quote|The final checkout is completed. All systems are operational. What course shall we set?''"
"''Perhaps she would respond to an alternative form of persuasion.''"
"''What do you mean?''"
"''I think it is time we demonstrated the full power of this station. Set your course for Alderaan.''"
"''With pleasure.|Admiral Motti, Grand Moff Tarkin, and Darth Vader|}} [[File:TarkinOrganaVader-ANH.png|thumb|300px|Motti looks on as Tarkin taunts Princess Leia Organa.]] Later, Motti supervised the final checkout of the battle station, showing that all systems were operational. The admiral went to [[Overbridge (Death Star I)|Overbridge]] to inform Tarkin, who, along with General Tagge, was being briefed by Lord Vader. The [[Sith]] [[Sith Lord|Lord]] had tortured the captive Leia with an [[IT-O interrogation droid|IT-O Interrogator droid]], though he was having difficulty extracting the location of the rebel's hidden base from her due to her formidable resistance to the mind probe. Upon arriving, Motti asked Tarkin what course the Death Star would take, who ordered it to head to Alderaan as a means for "alternate persuasion." Motti replied that he would do it with pleasure. Shortly thereafter, Motti approached the Grand Moff in private, once again expressing the extraordinary capabilities of the Death Star. This time, he noted that the ultimate power in the universe now rested with Tarkin, as he was in command of the battle station. Motti pointed out that the Grand Moff could, if willing, assume a position of authority in the Empire second only to the Emperor, subtly suggesting that he himself could serve with Tarkin. For his part, Tarkin regarded Motti's words as near treasonous and rejected the overture, though the ambitious Motti was not deterred from the idea.{{StoryCite|story=Verge of Greatness|book=From a Certain Point of View}} When the Death Star arrived in the [[Alderaan system]], Vader escorted Princess Leia to the Overbridge where Motti and Tarkin were. As the admiral looked on, Tarkin openly threatened to destroy Alderaan if Leia did not reveal to him the location of the Rebel's hidden base. In response to the threat of her home planet's destruction, she lied and informed the Grand Moff that the rebels were headquartered at the now-defunct [[Dantooine base|base]]''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' on [[Dantooine]]. Nonetheless, Tarkin ordered Motti to have the Death Star's superlaser [[Destruction of Alderaan|fire]] when ready, which shocked the princess. Motti did as ordered, and the Death Star fired on Alderaan, [[Destruction of Alderaan|destroying]] it within moments. Following the failed attempt at destroying Rango Tan, Tarkin had ordered Motti to install [[bio-tracker]]s in the [[helmet]]s of every Death Star gunner. This allowed the Grand Moff to discover that several gunners, such as [[Chief Gunner]] [[Endo Frant]], had hesitated at key points during the destruction of Alderaan, which resulted in their immediate shutting in an airlock and jettisoning into space. ====Death==== {{Quote|Rebel base one minute and closing.|An announcement made while Motti was on the Overbridge|}} [[File:Overbridge.jpg|thumb|left|290px|Motti stood on the Overbridge as the Death Star closed in on the rebel's hidden base.]] Shortly after Alderaan's destruction, General Tagge led a search on Dantooine, finding only an abandoned base. Though Tarkin ordered Leia to be executed, the order was not carried out. A [[YT-1300 light freighter]], the [[Millennium Falcon|''Millennium Falcon'']], made it aboard the Death Star and its crew [[Rescue of Princess Leia|succeeded]] in rescuing Organa from her [[Detention Block AA-23|cell]]. Earlier, when Vader had captured the ''Tantive IV'' over the planet [[Tatooine]], Leia passed the Death Star plans onto the [[astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]], who, along with [[C-3PO]], escaped the ''Tantive'' in an [[escape pod]] onto Tatooine's surface. There, they met [[Luke Skywalker]], a [[moisture farmer]]; [[Han Solo]], the ''Millennium'' ''Falcon''{{'s}} captain; [[Chewbacca]], Solo's [[First Mate|first mate]]; and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], a former [[Jedi Master]]. Initially, they planned on meeting with Leia's father, Imperial [[Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]], on Alderaan and give him the plans, but the planet's destruction and Organa's death changed their trajectory. The team managed to escape the battle station, but not before Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s had placed a [[Homing beacon|tracking device]] aboard the starship. The Empire managed to track the [[freighter]] to the Rebel base on the [[Moon|fourth moon]] of the planet [[Yavin Prime|Yavin]], and, as the Death Star prepared to destroy Yavin 4, a [[Battle of Yavin|battle]] began between the Imperial and Rebel forces above the Death Star. When several [[T-65 X-wing starfighter]]s proved adept at evading the station's defenses, Vader manned his [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced|personal]] [[TIE Advanced x1]] and attacked them. He began picking off the surviving fighters one by one, but [[Moradmin Bast|some]] [[officer]]s became worried that the rebel attack posed a danger, all while the battle station closed in on the rebel base. Motti stood beside the gunner on the Overbridge as it did so. However, the Alliance was aware of a flaw in the Death Star–a small, uncovered [[thermal exhaust port]] leading directly to the station's [[Reactor|main reactor]]. Against all odds, a Rebel X-wing piloted by Luke Skywalker succeeded in flying through the trench where the exhaust port was located, and successfully fired a pair of [[proton torpedo]]es into the shaft, causing the Death Star to explode, instantly killing all those on board, Motti included. ===Legacy=== [[3 ABY|Three]] [[Standard year|years]] after Motti's death, Vader recalled the moment he Force choked Motti after Palpatine punished him with the same method due to Vader's failures in turning Luke Skywalker, his son, to the [[dark side of the Force]] and for letting the [[Amidalans]] escape.[[Darth Vader (2020) 6|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 6]] ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|This isn't the first time you've spoken in this fashion, Motti.|Grand Moff Tarkin on Motti's growing ambition|}} [[File:Motti_calm.jpg|thumb|250px|left|The ambitious Imperial officer Admiral Motti saw the Death Star as the ultimate power in the universe.]] Loyal to Grand Moff Tarkin, Motti held a rivalry against Darth Vader. His ambition at times overrode his loyalty to the Empire, as evidenced in his approaching Tarkin to use the Death Star in a bid for power—where Motti himself would be at Tarkin's right hand. This ambition was partially borne out of his faith in the Death Star as an instrument of ultimate power; he believed the battle station to be invulnerable and considered that any rebel attack against would be a useless gesture doomed to fail. In this sense, he was vocally critical of views such as those of General Tagge concerning a credible rebel threat, colorfully stating that "the dog nipping at [Tagge's] heels is no threat to my locked and guarded house"—referring to the Death Star. More generally, Motti was dismissive of the rebellion as a whole, viewing the Alliance's military capabilities as nothing more than a "patchwork of X- and Y-wing fighters". According to Leia Organa, Motti enjoyed one of the largest egos in the galaxy.''[[A New Hope: The Princess, the Scoundrel, and the Farm Boy]]'' His arrogance was visible in his condescension towards other high-ranking officers, and in his submission of a lengthy and strongly-worded report on the strangulation incident between him and Darth Vader. Despite having been on the receiving end of the Sith Lord's displeasure, Motti remained unrepentant, insisting that Vader was the one at fault for using violence—a fact Motti interpreted as meaning he had won the argument. He further insinuated that Vader and Tagge were disloyal to the Empire, the former for putting his faith in the Force over the Death Star and the latter for being overly-concerned with the strength of the Rebellion. Although Motti claimed himself to be personally religious, he was also dismissive of the Force and doubted its very existence. He publicly regarded Darth Vader as a mere sorcerer with a "sad devotion" to an "ancient religion," later justifying his attitude as a response to alleged "workplace proselytization." This nearly resulted in his death when Vader Force-choked him for his insolence. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Oh yes. I was fortunate I was sent a complete script! A lot of people weren't sent complete scripts of the first film, they were sent a few pages. I'd actually read it and thought 'God, this is just so hard to get through!' It was 155 pages. It was so detailed with the descriptions and the dialogue was not very good. If you got through the script, it was such a good story that I thought 'OK, this could work.' I thought 'I know they could do this,' because they wouldn't make it if they couldn't do the special effects.|Richard LeParmentier, commenting on his ''A New Hope'' script|{{InsiderCite|96|The Men Who Built the Empire}}}} Motti first appeared in the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]]. He was played by [[Richard LeParmentier]], who was credited as "General Motti." Motti was originally intended to be an admiral, but as LeParmentier proved to be too tall for the uniform that he was to wear, he was fitted in the uniform of a general and Motti's rank was changed.{{InsiderCite|40|In the Star Wars Universe|In the ''Star Wars'' Universe: Richard LeParmentier}} [[File:Richard_LeParmentier.jpg|thumb|200px|Motti was portrayed by American actor Richard LeParmentier.]] LeParmentier originally auditioned for the role of [[Han Solo]], but lost out to [[Harrison Ford]]. He was then offered the role of a customs officer who would try to stop Solo from leaving Mos Eisley. A friend of LeParmentier took the part, but the role was ultimately cut from the film, yet LeParmentier was invited back one month later to read for Motti's part.{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsinterviews.com/original-trilogy/episode-iv-a-new-hope/richard-leparmentier-admiral-motti|text=Richard LeParmentier interview|archivedate=20161220062924|nolive=1}} An American actor, LeParmentier was one of the few non-English actors cast as Imperial officers who spoke without an English accent.{{Film|V}}{{Film|VI}} During filming, LeParmentier proposed director [[George Lucas]] to do his [[Wikipedia:Mid-Atlantic accent|Mid-Atlantic accent]] for Motti and Lucas accepted. To shoot the scene where Motti gets Force-choked by Darth Vader, LeParmentier spent days practicing choking in his dressing room to make it look convincing until he was able to control and induce spasms in his neck. While filming the scene, LeParmentier had his pants rolled up to his knees and took his boots off along with [[Don Henderson]] as it was really hot. In retrospective, Richard LeParmentier liked to be remembered as Motti, considering that it was an honor to have been part of the ''Star Wars'' saga.{{WebCite|url=http://www.admiralmotti.co.uk|text=Admiral Motti|archivedate=20161022100837}} In his opinion, ''A New Hope'' helped him to be offered more roles in some other big movies because it was the most memorable film he had been. LeParmentier was proud of the fact that Motti's Force choke was the first point in the saga that fans saw working the power of the Force, although back at that time, he had no idea if the film was to be as successful as it ultimately turned out. He greatly enjoyed his experience and cited the only inconvenience he faced on set was Motti's boots, as they caused him a considerable amount of foot perspiration. As such, the film's crewmembers would take the boots of the Imperials off and air-dry their feet between shots. While portraying the character, Richard LeParmentier saw Motti as a trigger-happy military type who was aching to demonstrate the Death Star's power and was resentful to the people who disagreed with him. He played Motti as a sanctimonious and smug character, believing that it was necessary in the contrast with the calm and reasonable Cassio Tagge played by Don Henderson to prompt Darth Vader to use the Force on Motti. By the time of his death in [[2013]], LeParmentier was producing an animated fan film called ''Motti Now'', in which Motti survives the Battle of Yavin and abandons the Empire. However, it is likely that he had not completed it prior to his death, as it has not been released as of yet. Motti was originally meant to appear, along with Generals Cassio Tagge and [[Trech Molock]], as one of the Imperials present at Tarkin's [[Imperial summit on Eriadu|summit]] on [[Eriadu]] in "[[The Summit]]," the fifteenth episode of the [[The Bad Batch Season 2|second season]] of the [[Disney+]] animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]''. However, it was eventually decided that the character would not have been high-ranking enough that early in the Empire's existence.{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/the-summit-episode-guide|text="The Summit" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}} ===Name origins=== {{Quote|See, because Lucas is the supreme creator of the Star Wars universe, ''when he says something it becomes real''. Oh yeah. I think you hear what I'm saying, party people: ''There is now officially a Star Wars character named after Conan!! HOW AWECELLET IS THAT?!'' The Star Wars wiki Wookieepedia has already incorporated the change into the Star Wars Mythology! Man! This week couldn't get any better!|Conan O'Brien's NBC blog|{{WebCite|url=https://blog.nbc.com/latenight/2007/05/breaking_hearts_and_making_far.php|text=Conan O'Brien's NBC.com blog|date=2008-05-02|work=NBC|archivedate=20080303214713}}}} Motti's full name was revealed by ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] on an episode of [[Wikipedia:Late Night with Conan O'Brien|''Late Night with Conan O'Brien'']] on [[May 1]], [[2007]]. When Lucas was challenged to a trivia question by a fan—''Late Night'' Associate Producer Jordan Schlansky—as to the name of the officer who Darth Vader Force chokes in ''A New Hope'', Lucas jokingly replied "Conan Antonio Motti," a [[tuckerization]] of [[Conan O'Brien]]'s name. The next day after the episode's airing, ''Late Night'' posted a blog entry on the NBC website about their surprise at the [[Special:Diff/1315629|quick response]] of [[Wookieepedia]] in adopting the new full name for Motti as well as their appreciation for Lucas' decision to name the character after O'Brien. The name was then confirmed in-universe by media relating to [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]], and later in the [[canon]] novel [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']]. ==Appearances== *[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] {{Ab|Tarkin (audiobook)}} {{1stID|Antonio}} *''[[Bounty Hunt]]'' *[[Age of Rebellion -
